newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF aims to settle insurance row with US this week.
newsitem.headline: MOF aims to settle insurance row with US this week.

text.p: Japan is aiming to solve its bilateral insurance dispute with the United States at talks to be held on Friday and Saturday, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Wednesday.

"The gap between the two sides remains large and I expect the negotiations to be difficult, but we will both cooperate to see what we can do and aim for a final solution at the next meeting," he said.
The talks on Friday and Saturday will be in Tokyo.
Mitsuzuka said his talks with Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky will start at 8 p.m. (1100 GMT) on Friday and will continue on Saturday morning.
Barshefsky will leave Japan on Saturday afternoon. "We will urge the United States to make a strong commitment towards resolving the issue as well as being flexible," he said.
On GDP figures released on Tuesday, he said that "overall, the data showed that the economic recovery is continuing".
Mitsuzuka said Japan will likely achieve the government's target of 2.5 percent economic growth this fiscal year.

Asked whether a supplementary budget with more public works spending would be needed to help the economy, Mitsuzuka said the government would take appropriate measures after looking at economic conditions and state finances.
The government will likely start drafting a supplementary budget after the current extraordinary session of parliament ends in about two weeks, he said.
Mitsuzuka also said he was asking the Liberal Democratic Party and two other parties with which it had a loose alliance to decide on proposed reforms of MOF by December 18.
The three parties had previously agreed to take the inspection and supervision functions of financial institutions away from the ministry and give them to an independent body.
Talks are being held within the LDP and among the parties on whether to go ahead with that idea and on how much independence any new body should be given.
They are also discussing who should be responsible for the new body.
